why: I compared the builder brief against the verifier's checks and probes, and the builder brief shares one of them. Step 2 gives an input with its expected output, "`node bin/greet.js --shout ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`". Verifier Check 1 uses the same pair: it runs `node bin/greet.js --shout ada` and its PASS condition cites "for example `HELLO, ADA!`". Step 7 tells the builder to run exactly that probe and "confirm the outputs". Running a command the expect line names is allowed, but handing over the verifier's concrete input and expected output is not. Other parts of the builder brief also mirror verifier probes. Step 3 covers the no-name case ("usage message and exit status 2"), which matches Check 2's `node bin/greet.js` invocation. Step 2 says the flag must work "before or after the name", which matches the advisory `node bin/greet.js ada --shout`. It also requires that `greeting(name)` stays unchanged, which matches the advisory note on src/greet.js. So the builder brief does not keep the verifier's methods private.
